newsitem.title: THAILAND: Central bank of Taiwan says monitoring Taiwan dlr.
newsitem.headline: Central bank of Taiwan says monitoring Taiwan dlr.

text.p: The Central Bank of Taiwan is monitoring the Taiwan dollar but at present has no plans to intervene in the market, its visiting governor Yuan-Dong Sheu told Reuters Financial Television on Friday.

Asked if the central bank was monitoring the situation in the foreign exchange markets bearing in mind the recent strength of the U.S. dollar, Sheu replied: "Yes we are monitoring...but at this moment we are not going to intervene."
The governor is here for the 32 Southeast Asian central bank governor's conference which ends later on Friday.
He added that the Taiwan dollar was still quite strong even though the U.S. dollar was getting stronger and stronger.
The Taiwan dollar was firmer early on Friday at T$27.536 against Thursday T$27.543 finish buoyed by an influx of foreign equity funds for the island's bullish stock market.
"If we continued to have such a strong Taiwan dollar, I think eventualy it will affect our exports. Since we are conducting financial liberalisation we let the market set the price," he said.
The Taiwan dollar has not fallen against the U.S. dollar significantly during the greenback's recent rally.

On February 4, as pre-Lunar New Year cash demand began to ease, the central bank issued a broad hint that it would not oppose a depreciation of the Taiwan dollar, saying it "in theory should reflect the U.S. dollar's prolonged overseas rise."
